control.docs: This is an [Action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions) for setting parameters for climate devices.

anova.docs:
The `anova` climate platform creates a climate device which can be used to control a BLE Anova sous-vide stick. Whilst not strictly a climate device, the concept of keeping something to a set temperature applies equally here.

*See also: [Anova Cooker](https://esphome.io/components/climate/anova)*

bang_bang.docs:
The `bang_bang` climate platform allows you to regulate a value with a [bang-bang controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang%E2%80%93bang_control) (also called hysteresis controller).

*See also: [Bang Bang Climate Controller](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bang_bang)*

bedjet.docs:
The `climate` platform exposes the BedJet's climate-related functionality, including setting the mode and target temperature.

*See also: [BedJet](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bedjet#bedjet-climate)*

haier.docs:
This is an implementation of the ESPHome component to control HVAC on the base of the SmartAir2 and hOn Haier protocols (AC that is controlled by the hOn or SmartAir2 application).

*See also: [Haier Climate](https://esphome.io/components/climate/haier)*

midea.docs:
The `midea` component creates a Midea air conditioner climate device.

*See also: [Midea Air Conditioner](https://esphome.io/components/climate/midea)*

mitsubishi_cn105.docs:
- **mitsubishi_cn105_id** (*Optional*, [ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)): The Mitsubishi CN105 hub to use.

*See also: [Mitsubishi CN105 Climate](https://esphome.io/components/climate/mitsubishi_cn105#climate)*

pid.docs:
The `pid` climate platform allows you to regulate a value with a [PID controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PID_controller).

*See also: [PID Climate](https://esphome.io/components/climate/pid)*

thermostat.docs:
The `thermostat` climate platform allows you to control a climate control system in much the same manner as a physical thermostat. Its operation is similar to the [Bang-Bang](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bang_bang/) controller; a sensor measures a value (the air temperature) and the controller will try to keep this value within a range defined by the set point(s). To do this, the controller can activate devices like a heating unit and/or a cooling unit to change the value observed by the sensor. When configured for both heating and cooling, it is essentially two [Bang-Bang](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bang_bang/) controllers in one; it differs, however, in that interaction with the thermostat component is nearly identical to that of a real thermostat.

*See also: [Thermostat Climate Controller](https://esphome.io/components/climate/thermostat)*

fan_mode.docs:
**string**: Set the fan mode of the climate device. One of `ON`, `OFF`, `AUTO`, `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `MIDDLE`, `FOCUS`, `DIFFUSE`, `QUIET`.

*See also: [Climate Component](https://esphome.io/components/climate#climatecontrol-action)*

id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The ID of the climate device to control.

*See also: [Climate Component](https://esphome.io/components/climate#climatecontrol-action)*

OFF.docs: The device is manually set to off, the device is inactive.

HEAT_COOL.docs: The device should heat/cool to maintain a target temperature.

COOL.docs: The device is set to cool to reach a target temperature.

HEAT.docs: The device is set to heat to reach a target temperature.

DRY.docs: The device is set to dry/humidity mode.

FAN_ONLY.docs: The device only has the fan enabled, no heating or cooling is taking place.

AUTO.docs: The device is should adjust the temperature dynamically. For example based on a schedule, or learned behavior.

*See also: [Climate Component](https://esphome.io/components/climate#base-climate-configuration)*

internal.docs:

*See also: [Climate Component](https://esphome.io/components/climate#base-climate-configuration)*
